This script plots survival, shell length, and condition index of each population in the field (final monitoring event, November 2024). Model results were generated by CR in `Q1_field_performance_models.Rmd`; condition index modeling by ZS.

Each figure shows all treatment groups with Lewisetta on the left and York River on the right, separated by a divider. Tukey compact-letter-display (CLD) groups are shown as a single token floating above each box: boxes that share a letter do not differ significantly. Because the CLD is computed across all site x population combinations at once, letters are comparable both within and between sites.

## Shared plotting setup

Everything the three figures have in common lives here: the population order, the
site colors, and a helper that draws the divided (Lewisetta | York River) boxplot
with floating CLD letters.

```{r}
# desired treatment-group order (used on both halves of every figure)
pop_order <- c("W1-TX", "W2-LA", "W3-FL", "W4-VA", "S1-LOLA", "S2-DEBY",
               "W5-NH", "W6-ME", "H1-HYBRIDMIX", "H2-SEEDMIX")

site_fill <- c("Lewisetta" = "#F06292", "YorkRiver" = "#880E4F")

# Build a divided boxplot with floating Tukey letters.
#   dat        : long data with columns  value, population, site (site = "Lewisetta"/"YorkRiver")
#   letters_df : one row per population x site, with columns population, site, group (the CLD letter)
#   The x-axis lays out Lewisetta 1..10, a gap, then York River 1..10, with a divider line.
plot_divided <- function(dat, letters_df, y_lab, subtitle_txt,
                         letter_gap = 0.04) {
  n <- length(pop_order)

  # numeric x position: Lewisetta 1..n on the left, York n+2..2n+1 on the right (gap at n+1)
  xpos <- tibble(
    population = factor(rep(pop_order, 2), levels = pop_order),
    site       = rep(c("Lewisetta", "YorkRiver"), each = n),
    x          = c(seq_len(n), seq_len(n) + n + 1)
  )

  dat <- dat %>%
    mutate(population = factor(population, levels = pop_order),
           site = factor(site, levels = c("Lewisetta", "YorkRiver"))) %>%
    left_join(xpos, by = c("population", "site"))

  # y position for each letter: just above the box's upper whisker
  span <- diff(range(dat$value, na.rm = TRUE))
  letter_pos <- dat %>%
    group_by(site, population, x) %>%
    summarise(y = quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) +
                  1.5 * IQR(value, na.rm = TRUE) + letter_gap * span,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(letters_df, by = c("population", "site"))

  # axis breaks at every box, labeled by population (both halves show the same names)
  breaks_x <- xpos$x
  labels_x <- as.character(xpos$population)

  ggplot(dat, aes(x = x, y = value, group = x, fill = site)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.7, linewidth = 0.4, fatten = 0.5, outlier.size = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = n + 1, color = "grey40") +           # divider
    geom_text(data = letter_pos, aes(x = x, y = y, label = group),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3, angle = 35) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks_x, labels = labels_x,
                       expand = expansion(add = 0.7)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = site_fill,
                      labels = c("Lewisetta" = "Lewisetta", "YorkRiver" = "York River"),
                      name = "Site") +
    labs(x = "Treatment group", y = y_lab, subtitle = subtitle_txt) +
    # annotate the two halves
    annotate("text", x = (1 + n) / 2, y = -Inf, label = "Lewisetta",
             vjust = 2.2, size = 3.6) +
    annotate("text", x = (n + 2 + 2 * n + 1) / 2, y = -Inf, label = "York River",
             vjust = 2.2, size = 3.6) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black", size = 9),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black", size = 10),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
          plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 22, 5.5))  # extra bottom room for site labels
}
```

## Condition Index

Condition index calculations and modeling by ZS. Site x population differences at
the final timepoint are tested with a Tukey CLD across all site x population combinations.

### Data preparation
```{r}
MVP_phenotyping_final <- read_csv("data/performance_H2F/MVP_phenotyping_final.csv",
                                  show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(population = as.character(population),
         population = if_else(population == "H1-LARMIX", "H1-HYBRIDMIX", population),
         population = factor(population, levels = pop_order))

data202411 <- MVP_phenotyping_final %>% filter(samplingTimePoint == "2024-11")
```

### Models and post-hoc testing
```{r}
mixed.model.3 <- lmer(CI ~ site * population + (1 | bagID), data = data202411)
mm3_anova <- Anova(mixed.model.3, type = 3)

# single model on the site x population combination, for pairwise CLD across all 20 groups
mixed.model.3.site.pop <- lmer(CI ~ site.pop + (1 | bagID), data = data202411)
mm3.emmeans <- emmeans(mixed.model.3.site.pop, pairwise ~ site.pop, adjust = "tukey")
mm3.cld <- cld(mm3.emmeans$emmeans, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, decreasing = TRUE)

# tidy the CLD into population x site + a clean letter token
site_pop_key <- data202411 %>%
  distinct(site.pop, site, population)

ci_letters <- as.data.frame(mm3.cld) %>%
  mutate(group = trimws(.group)) %>%
  left_join(site_pop_key, by = "site.pop") %>%
  # site in the CI data is coded LEW / YR; recode to match the plot helper
  mutate(site = dplyr::recode(as.character(site), "LEW" = "Lewisetta", "YR" = "YorkRiver")) %>%
  dplyr::select(population, site, group)
```

### Model with time inclusion + save results
```{r}
mixed.model.4 <- lmer(CI ~ site * population * samplingTimePoint + (1 | bagID),
                      data = MVP_phenotyping_final %>%
                        filter(samplingTimePoint %in% c("2024-05", "2024-11")))

sink("results/performance_H2F/Q1_condition_model_results.txt")
cat("Mixed model 3: CI ~ site * population + (1|bagID)\n\n")
print(summary(mixed.model.3))
cat("\n\nType III Wald chi-square tests\n\n")
print(mm3_anova)
cat("\n\nPairwise comparisons: site.pop (Tukey-adjusted)\n\n")
print(mm3.emmeans)
cat("\n\nMixed model 4: CI ~ site * population * timepoint + (1|bagID)\n\n")
print(anova(mixed.model.4))
cat("\n\nStep reduction\n\n")
print(step(mixed.model.4))
sink()
```

### Figure product
```{r}
ci_plot_df <- data202411 %>%
  mutate(site = dplyr::recode(as.character(site), "LEW" = "Lewisetta", "YR" = "YorkRiver")) %>%
  transmute(value = CI, population, site)

field_ci <- plot_divided(
  dat          = ci_plot_df,
  letters_df   = ci_letters,
  y_lab        = "Condition index",
  subtitle_txt = "Final field monitoring event, November 2024"
)
field_ci

ggsave("FigS4_field_ci.pdf", plot = field_ci, device = "pdf",
       path = "figures/performance_H2F", height = 5, width = 9)
```

## Survival

Survival modeling by CR; CLD letters are read from the model-results CSV (column `letters`).

```{r}
survival <- read.csv("data/performance_H2F/field_surv_final_time.csv")[, -c(1, 8)]
colnames(survival) <- c("pop_site", "site", "population", "bag_label", "t", "survival", "letters")

# long data for plotting
surv_plot_df <- survival %>%
  transmute(value = survival, population, site)

# one CLD letter per population x site (letters are pre-computed in the CSV)
surv_letters <- survival %>%
  distinct(population, site, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  transmute(population, site, group = trimws(letters))
```

```{r}
field_surv <- plot_divided(
  dat          = surv_plot_df,
  letters_df   = surv_letters,
  y_lab        = "Survival",
  subtitle_txt = "Final field monitoring event, November 2024"
)
field_surv

ggsave("Fig2B_field_surv.pdf", plot = field_surv, device = "pdf",
       path = "figures/performance_H2F", height = 5, width = 9)
```

## Length

Length modeling by CR; CLD letters are read from the model-results CSV (column `letters`).

```{r}
length <- read.csv("data/performance_H2F/field_length_final_time.csv")[, 2:10]
colnames(length) <- c("pop_site", "bag_site", "pop", "t", "bags_label",
                      "tags_label", "length", "width", "letters")

len_plot_df <- length %>%
  transmute(value = length, population = pop, site = bag_site)

len_letters <- length %>%
  distinct(pop, bag_site, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  transmute(population = pop, site = bag_site, group = trimws(letters))
```

```{r}
field_len <- plot_divided(
  dat          = len_plot_df,
  letters_df   = len_letters,
  y_lab        = "Length (mm)",
  subtitle_txt = "Final field monitoring event, November 2024"
)
field_len

ggsave("Fig2C_field_len.pdf", plot = field_len, device = "pdf",
       path = "figures/performance_H2F", height = 5, width = 9)
```
